setup_lead: This app doesn't have its own account. Instead, your mods live in a (free) GitHub account. This one-time setup connects the app to GitHub so it can back up and publish what you make.
setup_credentials_lead: The GitHub sign-in registered on this computer. Used for backing up and publishing your mods.
setup_switch_confirm: This makes your computer forget the saved GitHub sign-in for github.com   system-wide, not just in this app. Every tool that uses it will be affected: the next git push, pull, or fetch (in any terminal, editor, or Git client), as well as publishing from this app, will prompt you to sign in again.
setup_forks_lead: Forks are your copies of the base content (mod templates) and the registry (list of published mods), saved to your GitHub account. You need these forks to create and publish mods.
setup_forks_unreachable: At least one saved fork could not be reached on GitHub. It may have been deleted or renamed - run setup again to recreate it.
setup_manual_intro: Create these forks in your browser, then run setup again:
setup_author_lead: Pre-filled when you create a new mod.
setup_clear_lead: Removes your saved fork locations and author details from this computer. Forgets your GitHub sign-in for this app, but does not affect your system-wide GitHub credentials for other tools.
setup_appearance_lead: Choose a theme, or use your system's default.
setup_advanced_lead: For creators comfortable with using git from the terminal. Reveals power-user tools on the mod's page.
setup_error_no_sign_in: Could not detect a GitHub sign-in. These tools push to GitHub over HTTPS, so an HTTPS sign-in is required. Set one up (Git Credential Manager will prompt you), then try again.
setup_error_switch_manual: Could not clear the saved GitHub credential automatically. Clear it yourself with `git credential reject`, then run setup again.
setup_commit_email: Commits will be made as {email} to protect your privacy.
identity_override_body: This will be committed as {name} <{email}>, not your local git config ({localName} <{localEmail}>).

conflict_explainer_body_1: Including other content merges incoming files into your mod. When your version and the incoming one both changed the same lines, the app can't tell which to keep. That's a conflict.
conflict_explainer_body_2: For each conflicted file you can choose: keep your version, or take the incoming one. Not sure? You can undo the whole merge and your mod will go back to how it was before you tried to include the new content.

help_panel_intro: New to modding Earthborne Rangers? Here's how it works:
help_panel_step_newmod: Use this app to make a new mod. It'll copy some initial entries into a folder to get you started.
help_panel_step_github: Your mod is saved to GitHub, which is a tool used for backing up and sharing code and other files. This app handles all the "git" stuff for you.
help_panel_step_obsidian: Write your mod's journal entries in the free note-taking app, Obsidian. You'll use Markdown to style your journal entries. Both are easy to learn and don't require any coding experience.
help_panel_step_publish: When it's ready, publish your mod from this app so players can find and play it.
help_panel_finally: For more details, like how to use Markdown to style your journal entries, or include custom cards, campaign trackers, or other files with your mod, see the online modding guide.
newmod_explainer_body: Next, launch Obsidian, and open "{dir}" as a vault. If you don't have Obsidian yet, it's free to download.
obsidian_unregistered_body: Obsidian doesn't know about this mod yet. Select "{open_command}" and use "Open folder as vault" to open "{dir}" in Obsidian.
